assumptions.condition: Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural action is \(A=A_{c_j(s)}\).
Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural outcome is \(Y=Y_{c_j(s)}\).
For every unit and configurations \(c=(r,q)\), \(c'=(r',q')\) in \(\mathcal C\), \(r=Z\) and \(r'\neq Z\) imply \(Y_c\ge Y_{c'}\).
For every unit, \(r=Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\le Y_{(r,q')}\).
For every unit, \(r\neq Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\ge Y_{(r,q')}\).
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(p\in\mathfrak O\).

definitions.name: Selective-Label Counterfactual-Correctness response-type class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{t=(s,z,(a_c),(y_c))\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{raw}}: y_{(z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q;\ y_{(z,q)}\le y_{(z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(1-z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q)}=y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q\}\).

definitions.name: Finite randomized selective-label SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{M: M\text{ has finite }\mathcal S,J,\mathcal Q,\text{ binary }Z,A,Y,\text{ and satisfies the randomized assignment, known arm-law, common-action, common-outcome, reveal-action, masked-truth, correctness, performance-order, and neutral-invariance conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Selective-label observable-law map
definitions.construction: For \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\) and \(t=(s_t,z_t,(a_c(t)),(y_c(t)))\), set \(B_{o,t}=\rho_j\mathbf 1\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,\ \ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\}\).

definitions.name: Ground-truth-blind comparison programs
definitions.construction: Apply \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to every observable cell and solve the same two programs with \(B_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) and right-hand side \(p_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\).

definitions.name: Finite-sample whole-set confidence construction
definitions.construction: Compute the Bonferroni simultaneous Clopper--Pearson box \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and intersect it with \(\mathfrak O\). When the intersection is nonempty, optimize \(h_e^{\top}v\) over \(v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) subject to \(Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\); when it is empty, return the total fallback interval \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: Euclidean-projection plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction: Project \(\widehat p\) onto \(\mathfrak O\) in Euclidean norm and evaluate both endpoint programs: \(\widehat\theta=\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\widehat p)\).

definitions.name: Projection-composed endpoint directional map
definitions.construction:
For a direction \(g\), put \(z=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Using the full unnormalized dual faces, define
\[
\Gamma'_p(g)=\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right).
\]
Only the slope coordinate acts on \(z\); no normalized representative is selected.

definitions.name: Active-cone and dual-face subsampling handle
definitions.construction: Within \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), enumerate boundary faces and retain the smallest face on which projection and both endpoint programs tie. Enumerate its active projection cones and optimal dual faces, compute the exact piecewise-linear Gaussian law of \(\max\{\Gamma'_{p,L}(G_p),-\Gamma'_{p,U}(G_p)\}\), and compare it with the centered without-replacement \(m_n\)-out-of-\(n\) critical value \(c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}\).

definitions.name: Strictly positive four-coordinate witness mixture
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), set \(\varepsilon_{32}=\pi_4/24\), \(a_{32}=\pi_2-\pi_4/8\), and \(b_{32}=\pi_1+\pi_2-\pi_4/8\). Assign weight \(\varepsilon_{32}\) to every table row except rows \(20\) and \(32\), assign \(a_{32}\) to row \(20\), and assign \(b_{32}\) to row \(32\). The induced full and blind laws are \(B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\) and \(K^{32}B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\).

definitions.name: Full and blind-embedded endpoint dual faces
definitions.construction:
With the simplex mass multiplier left explicit, define
\[
\mathcal D_L=\{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{|\mathcal O|}:\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\leq h_e\},
\qquad
\mathcal D_U=\{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{|\mathcal O|}:\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\geq h_e\}.
\]
For \(p\in\mathfrak O\), define the unnormalized full optimal faces
\[
\Lambda_L(p)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\qquad
\Lambda_U(p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\}.
\]
Finally, writing \(d_K\) for the number of rows of \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\), define the embedded blind-dual subspace
\[
\mathcal E_K=\{(\alpha,K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu):
\alpha\in\mathbb R,\ \mu\in\mathbb R^{d_K}\}.
\]

definitions.name: Primitive bracket-stratum design condition
definitions.construction:
The primitive bracket-stratum condition \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) holds when there are \(s_*\in\mathcal S\) and \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\) in \(\mathcal Q\) such that
\[
c_e(s_*)=(1,q_m),\qquad
c_j(s_*)\in\{(1,q_\ell),(1,q_h)\}\quad(j\in J_0),
\]
at least one trial arm uses \((1,q_\ell)\), at least one trial arm uses \((1,q_h)\), and \(\rho_j>0\) for every \(j\in J_0\).  No restriction is placed on other strata, on configurations away from \(s_*\), or on additional elements of \(\mathcal Q\).

statements.statement: The observable--target image of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) is exactly \(\{(Bw,h_e^{\top}w):w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}\). In the forward direction, every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) induces its distribution over legal deterministic response types. In the converse direction, every \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) canonically defines an attaining SCM \(M_w\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) by drawing \(t\sim w\), independently drawing \(D\sim\rho\), and reading the structural responses from \(t\).
statements.justification: The converse is the substantive bridge from every feasible latent optimizer to a legally realized human--AI SCM.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1, give the general discrete response-function construction; this theorem identifies the exact quotient required by action-dependent truth revelation and the ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 common \(q\)-indexed order restrictions.
statements.consumer: It licenses sharp evaluation of an untrialed PSA or assisted-decision policy without treating an algebraic completion as a causal model.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) and define
\[
T=\bigl(S,Z,(A_c)_{c\in\mathcal C},(Y_c)_{c\in\mathcal C}\bigr),\qquad
w_t=\Pr_M(T=t).
\]
The four unit-level restrictions imply the four membership conditions in \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\), so \(T\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) almost surely.  Thus \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).

Fix \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\).  Randomized assignment and the known arm law give \(\Pr(D=j,T=t)=\rho_jw_t\).  Conditional on \(D=j,T=t\), the common-response assumptions give \(A=a_{c_j(s)}(t)\) and \(Y=y_{c_j(s)}(t)\) on \(S=s\).  Revelation and masking give \(\ell=z_t\) when \(a=1\) and \(\ell=\star\) when \(a=0\).  Hence, by the incidence definition,
\[
\Pr_M(O_i=o)
=\sum_t\rho_jw_t\mathbf 1\!\left\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,\
\ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\right\}
=\sum_tB_{o,t}w_t.
\]
Therefore \(p=Bw\).  The target definition gives
\[
\tau_e(M)=\mathbb E_M[Y_{c_e(S)}]
=\sum_tw_ty_{c_e(s_t)}(t)=h_e^{\top}w.
\]

Conversely, fix \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Draw \(T=t\) with probability \(w_t\), independently draw \(D=j\) with probability \(\rho_j\), and define \(S,Z,(A_c),(Y_c)\) by the coordinates of \(T\).  Under policy \(j\), set \(A=A_{c_j(S)}\), \(Y=Y_{c_j(S)}\), \(R=A\), and set \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) on \(R=1\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) on \(R=0\).  This construction satisfies randomized assignment, the known arm law, both common-response restrictions, revelation, and masking.  Every supported type is legal, so all four outcome restrictions hold.  Consequently \(M_w\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  The preceding calculation gives observable law \(Bw\) and target \(h_e^{\top}w\), proving both inclusions.

statements.statement: As a corollary of \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), for every \(p\in\mathfrak O\) the identified set of \(\tau_e\) is \([L(p),U(p)]\); compactness attains both endpoints and mixtures of endpoint SCMs attain every intermediate value.
statements.justification: This corollary records the causal interpretation of the two programs without treating LP compactness as the novelty kernel.
statements.gap: The generic optimization implication is informed by DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024; the application-specific advance is carried by the complete strict-refinement certificate.
statements.consumer: It converts each reported LP interval into the exact set of deployment means compatible with the model.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\) and let
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\}.
\]
This fiber is nonempty, convex, and compact.  By \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), its compatible causal values are exactly
\[
\{\tau_e(M):P_M(O_i)=p,\ M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
=\{h_e^{\top}v:v\in F(p)\}.
\]
The continuous linear image of a compact convex set in \(\mathbb R\) is a compact interval.  Its attained endpoints are \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\) by \(\text{def:sharp-endpoint-programs}\).  If \(v_L,v_U\) attain them, then, for \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\),
\[
v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)v_L+\gamma v_U\in F(p),\qquad
h_e^{\top}v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)L(p)+\gamma U(p).
\]
The converse theorem constructs an SCM for every \(v_\gamma\), so the identified set is exactly \([L(p),U(p)]\).

statements.statement: For every \(p\in\mathfrak O\), feasibility under \(Bv=p\) implies feasibility under \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\), hence \([L(p),U(p)]\subseteq[L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)]\).
statements.justification: The one-line coarsening fact fixes the direction of comparison used by the strict certificate.
statements.gap: This is a data-processing lemma, not a claim to extend LakkarajuKleinbergLeskovecLudwigMullainathan2017.
statements.consumer: It makes any strict endpoint gap interpretable as information supplied by selectively revealed labels.
statements.proof_tex:
Define
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\},\qquad
F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\}.
\]
Applying \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to \(Bv=p\) proves \(F(p)\subseteq F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\).  Minimization over the larger set cannot increase, and maximization cannot decrease.  Therefore
\[
L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\leq L(p)\leq U(p)
\leq U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),
\]
which is the asserted inclusion.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\), all thirty-two rows of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) are distinct members of \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\). When \(z=0\), the neutral outcomes are constant at one and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nonincreasing; when \(z=1\), the neutral outcomes are constant at zero and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nondecreasing, so correctness, both performance orders, and neutrality hold row by row. Under the specialization, \(B^{32}\) reads only the action and outcome coordinates at the two trialed configurations \((1,q_{\ell})\) and \((1,q_h)\), together with the label when an endpoint action reveals it, whereas \(h^{32}\) reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\). Thus \(A_{(1,q_m)}\) is free in the observable--target quotient even though the untrialed policy uses it to define deployment action: \(e_{32}\) is absent from the trial incidence map, and the target is outcome-only. Every action coordinate at any other nontrialed configuration is likewise free. Since legal response types impose outcome restrictions but no cross-coordinate action restriction, these free actions may be fixed to the displayed values without changing \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\), \(h^{32}(t)\), or \(K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\). Every legal full response type has the same observable--target pair as at least one displayed row, because its restricted outcome path has a displayed representative and the four displayed patterns exhaust the two endpoint action bits. Hence the thirty-two displayed combinations form a complete quotient-generating cover; no injectivity or minimality is asserted. The twelve displayed cells are every feasible observable row and each occurs in the table. Consequently the table generates the full observable polytope and cannot omit a column that changes any of the four optima. For every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), the programs formed with \(B^{32}\), \(h^{32}\), and \(K^{32}\) satisfy \(L=\pi_1+\pi_2\), \(U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4\), \(L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1\), and \(U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1\). Thus \(p^{32}\) gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\), while \(p^{32,\circ}\) gives \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\). Both laws lie in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\), since their displayed mixtures give strictly positive weight to every generator of \(\mathfrak O^{32}=B^{32}\Delta_{31}\).
statements.justification: The complete quotient-generating cover, positive generating mixture, and exact arithmetic establish a legally realized and non-boundary two-sided gain without claiming that the displayed cover is injective or minimal.
statements.gap: ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 reports narrower simulated bounds but gives no sharp action-dependent selective-label quotient-generating cover, exact rational full-versus-blind certificate, or full-polytope relative-interior realization.
statements.consumer: The table is an exact regression fixture for the Imai PSA and aihuman implementations, including every reveal-action pattern and both performance-order directions.
statements.proof_tex:
Use the row and column orders fixed by \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\).  We first verify legality and the observable--target cover.  For a row with \(z=0\), the displayed neutral-outcome triple is \(111\), and the displayed \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\qquad 100,\qquad 110,\qquad 111.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus the neutral outcome is constant, the \(r=1\) outcome is nonincreasing in \(q\), and the neutral outcome is at least every \(r=1\) outcome.  These are respectively neutral invariance, incorrect-performance order, and counterfactual correctness from \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\); correct-performance order is automatic because the correct neutral path is constant.  For a row with \(z=1\), the displayed neutral triple is \(000\), and the displayed \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\qquad 001,\qquad 011,\qquad 111.
\tag{20}
\]
Now the neutral outcome is constant, the correct \(r=1\) outcome is nondecreasing, and every \(r=1\) outcome is at least the neutral outcome.  Hence all four restrictions in \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\) again hold.  The action array is unrestricted by that definition.  The displayed arrays and labels differ wherever their row indices differ, so the thirty-two rows are distinct legal full response types.

For completeness, let \(t\) be any legal response type in the specialized design.  Since \(\mathcal S^{32}=\{s_0\}\), its stratum is \(s_0\).  By \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\) and the incidence-column construction in \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\), \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\) reads only
\[
\bigl(A_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_\ell)}\bigr),
\qquad
\bigl(A_{(1,q_h)},Y_{(1,q_h)}\bigr),
\tag{21}
\]
together with \(z\) in an endpoint cell for which the corresponding action equals one.  The target coordinate \(h^{32}(t)\) reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\).  In particular, it does not read \(A_{(1,q_m)}\).  Although the untrialed policy uses \((1,q_m)\) to define its deployment action, \(e_{32}\notin J^{32}_0\), so that action is absent from the trial incidence map; the target is outcome-only, so it is absent from \(h^{32}\) as well.  The same is true of every action coordinate at a configuration not used by a trial arm.  Since \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\) imposes restrictions only on outcomes and no cross-coordinate restriction on actions, all such action coordinates may be fixed to their displayed values without changing \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\), \(h^{32}(t)\), or \(K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\).

It remains to cover the outcomes read in (21) and by the target.  If \(z=0\), neutral invariance makes the correct neutral triple constant.  When that constant is zero, correctness forces the incorrect \(r=1\) triple to be \(000\); when it is one, incorrect-performance order permits exactly the four paths in (19).  The omitted neutral-zero case has the same read coordinates as the displayed representative with \(r=1\) path \(000\).  If \(z=1\), the incorrect neutral triple is constant.  When that constant is one, correctness forces the correct \(r=1\) triple to be \(111\); when it is zero, correct-performance order permits exactly the four paths in (20).  The omitted neutral-one case has the same read coordinates as the displayed representative with \(r=1\) path \(111\).  Finally, the four displayed endpoint-action patterns exhaust
\[
\bigl(A_{(1,q_\ell)},A_{(1,q_h)}\bigr)\in\{0,1\}^2.
\tag{22}
\]
Thus every legal response type has the same \((B^{32}_{\cdot,t},h^{32}(t))\), and hence the same \((K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t},h^{32}(t))\), as at least one displayed row.  This is a complete quotient-generating cover; no injectivity or minimality is asserted.  Indeed, rows \(1\) and \(17\) have the same observable column and target because both endpoint actions are zero and both read endpoint outcomes and the middle outcome are zero.  Inspection of the table also shows that each of the six possible cells in each trial arm occurs.  Therefore the twelve displayed cells are exactly the feasible observable rows, and the listed columns generate the full observable polytope without omitting a column that can alter any of the four endpoint programs.

We next calculate those programs.  For \(\pi_3=\pi_2\), direct multiplication of the weights in \(\text{def:32-coordinate-mixture}\) by the two half-incidence entries in every table column gives
\[
\begin{split}
p(\pi)=\bigl(&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/24,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24,\pi_4/8,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\\
&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/8,\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\pi_4/24,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24\bigr)^{\top},
\end{split}
\tag{23}
\]
and coarsening the two revealed-label cells with equal action and outcome gives
\[
K^{32}p(\pi)=\bigl(\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,
\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12\bigr)^{\top}.
\tag{24}
\]
In the full and blind row orders, respectively, define
\[
\lambda_L=(0,0,0,0,0,2,0,0,0,0,2,0)^{\top},
\]
\[
\lambda_U=(0,0,-2,0,0,0,2,2,2,0,2,2)^{\top},
\]
\[
\mu_L=(0,2,0,2,-2,0,-2,0)^{\top},
\qquad
\mu_U=(2,2,2,2,0,0,0,0)^{\top}.
\tag{25}
\]
For each displayed column \(i\), the monotone paths (19)--(20) imply
\[
\lambda_L^{\top}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}\leq h^{32}_i
\leq\lambda_U^{\top}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}.
\tag{26}
\]
For the lower inequality, the left side is the indicator of the low-arm cell \((1,1,1)\) plus the indicator of the high-arm cell \((1,1,0)\); only the summand matching the unit's label can be nonzero, and endpoint monotonicity then forces the middle outcome to one.  For the upper inequality, when \(z=0\) the right side is \(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_\ell)}=1,Y_{(1,q_\ell)}=0\}\), and when \(z=1\) it is \(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_h)}=1,Y_{(1,q_h)}=0\}\).  In either case a middle outcome of one forces the relevant endpoint outcome to one by the appropriate performance order.  Similarly, column by column,
\[
\mu_L^{\top}K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}
=Y_{(1,q_\ell)}(t_i^{32})+Y_{(1,q_h)}(t_i^{32})-1
\leq h_i^{32}
\leq 1
=\mu_U^{\top}K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}.
\tag{27}
\]
The left inequality holds for every binary monotone three-point path: if both endpoint values are one, the middle value is one, and otherwise the left side is nonpositive.  The quotient-generating cover already proved shows that every omitted legal column has the same incidence and target entries as a displayed column, so (26)--(27) hold for every legal column.  With simplex multiplier \(\alpha=0\), they are therefore feasible dual certificates.  Indeed, for any \(v\geq0\) with \(\mathbf 1^{\top}v=1\) and \(B^{32}v=p(\pi)\), multiplying (26) by \(v_i\) and summing gives
\[
\lambda_L^{\top}p(\pi)\leq (h^{32})^{\top}v
\leq\lambda_U^{\top}p(\pi).
\]
The identical calculation using (27) applies to every blind-feasible \(v\).  Substitution of (23)--(24) therefore yields
\[
L\geq\pi_1+\pi_2,\qquad
U\leq\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,\qquad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}\geq\pi_1,\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}\leq1.
\tag{28}
\]

For matching primal certificates, notation \(\{i:x,\ldots\}\) lists the nonzero coordinates of a nonnegative vector.  Put \(r_1=(1,0,0)\), \(r_2=(0,1,0)\), and \(r_3=(0,1,8)\) in \((\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_4)\)-coordinates, and let \(P(r_k)\) denote the linear expression on the right side of (23) evaluated at \(r_k\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|l}
X&v_1^X&v_2^X&v_3^X\\\hline
FL&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,6:2,7:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,21:2/3,22:5/3,23:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
FU&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,10:2,11:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,25:2/3,26:5/3,27:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
BL&\{32:1\}&\{8:1,24:1\}&
\{5:8/3,8:7/3,21:8/3,24:7/3\}\\
BU&\{32:1\}&\{12:1,28:1\}&
\{9:8/3,12:7/3,25:8/3,28:7/3\}.
\end{array}
\tag{29}
\]
Adding the two half-incidence entries of every listed column verifies, for \(k=1,2,3\),
\[
B^{32}v_k^{FL}=B^{32}v_k^{FU}=P(r_k),
\qquad
K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BL}=K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BU}=K^{32}P(r_k).
\tag{30}
\]
The masses of the vectors for \(k=1,2,3\) are \(1,2,10\), and their target sums are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_1^X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_2^X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_3^X\\\hline
FL&1&1&1\\
FU&1&1&9\\
BL&1&0&0\\
BU&1&2&10.
\end{array}
\tag{31}
\]
For \(X\in\{FL,FU,BL,BU\}\), set
\[
v^X(\pi)=\pi_1v_1^X+\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)v_2^X
+\frac{\pi_4}{8}v_3^X.
\tag{32}
\]
The coefficients are nonnegative because \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\) entails \(\pi_1>0\), \(\pi_4>0\), and \(\pi_2>\pi_4/8\).  Using \(\pi_3=\pi_2\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^4\pi_k=1\), its mass is
\[
\pi_1+2\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)
+10\frac{\pi_4}{8}
=\pi_1+2\pi_2+\pi_4=1.
\tag{33}
\]
Moreover,
\[
(\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_4)
=\pi_1r_1+\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)r_2
+\frac{\pi_4}{8}r_3.
\tag{34}
\]
Equations (30), (33), and (34) prove primal feasibility of the four vectors in (32), and (31) gives objectives \(\pi_1+\pi_2\), \(\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4\), \(\pi_1\), and \(1\), respectively.  These reverse the four inequalities in (28), so
\[
L=\pi_1+\pi_2,\qquad
U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,\qquad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1,\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1.
\tag{35}
\]
At \(\pi^{32}=(1,1,1,1)^{\top}/4\), (35) gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\), and (23) gives the stated vector \(p^{32}\).  At \(\pi^{32,\circ}=(198,199,199,204)^{\top}/800\), it gives \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\), and (23) gives the stated vector \(p^{32,\circ}\).

Finally, for every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\),
\[
\varepsilon_{32}=\frac{\pi_4}{24}>0,
\qquad
a_{32}=\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}>0,
\qquad
b_{32}=\pi_1+a_{32}>0.
\tag{36}
\]
Also \(30\varepsilon_{32}+a_{32}+b_{32}=\pi_1+2\pi_2+\pi_4=1\), so \(w^{32}(\pi)\) is a probability vector assigning positive weight to every displayed generator.  To verify relative interior directly, aggregate the positive weights of duplicate columns and enumerate the distinct columns as \(b_1,\ldots,b_N\), with aggregate weights \(\beta_k>0\).  Let \(V=\operatorname{span}\{b_k-b_1:2\leq k\leq N\}\), the direction space of \(\operatorname{aff}(\mathfrak O^{32})\), and define the surjective linear map
\[
T:\{x\in\mathbb R^N:\mathbf 1^{\top}x=0\}\longrightarrow V,
\qquad T(x)=\sum_{k=1}^N x_kb_k.
\]
Choose a linear right inverse \(R:V\to\{x:\mathbf 1^{\top}x=0\}\).  If \(V\neq\{0\}\), its finite-dimensional operator norm \(C=\sup_{\|d\|_2=1}\|Rd\|_\infty\) is finite.  Hence whenever \(\|d\|_2<\min_k\beta_k/C\), the vector \(\beta+Rd\) is nonnegative, has mass one, and maps to \(\sum_k\beta_kb_k+d\).  If \(V=\{0\}\), the relative domain is a singleton and the conclusion is immediate.  Thus the mixture has a neighborhood in the affine hull contained in \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), proving that it lies in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).  This applies to both displayed choices of \(\pi\).  By \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), each feasible primal vector in (32) canonically constructs a legal SCM attaining its objective.  Thus (35) gives sharp causal endpoints, not merely extrema of an unrelated regression program.

statements.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal U\subset\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\) containing \(p^{32,\circ}\) such that \(L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) and \(U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal U\). The conclusion follows from the two strict gaps \(199/800\) at \(p^{32,\circ}\) and continuity of the four finite-polyhedral value functions on relative interior.
statements.justification: This is the balanced thirty-two-type corollary of the general dual-face characterization and primitive bracket-stratum theorem.
statements.gap: The general theorem, rather than this corollary alone, supplies the arbitrary-finite-design characterization absent from the comparison literature.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts retain the exact rational regression fixture and a stable local neighborhood for implementation checks.
statements.proof_tex:
The singleton-stratum balanced design of \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\) satisfies \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\): take \(s_*=s_0\), use \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\), and note that its two trial arms have probabilities \(1/2>0\).  The exact certificate gives, at \(p_0=p^{32,\circ}\),
\[
L(p_0)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)=\frac{199}{800},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)-U(p_0)=\frac{199}{800}.
\]
By \(\text{thm:general-dual-face-strict-refinement-characterization}\), the strict region is relatively open on the whole observable polytope.  Since the exact certificate also gives \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\), the intersection of that strict region with a sufficiently small relative neighborhood of \(p_0\) inside \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\) is the required nonempty set \(\mathcal U\).

statements.statement: Applying the generic simultaneous-region propagation of DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, to the SLCC incidence program gives \(\Pr_p\{[L(p),U(p)]\subseteq\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(p\in\mathfrak O\). On \(p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), the intersection \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathfrak O\) is nonempty and the implementation optima are attained.
statements.justification: This implementation corollary supplies an exact conservative reporting procedure while acknowledging the generic propagation theorem as prior art.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, already establish generic confidence-region propagation; the contribution here is its explicit implementation for the SLCC incidence map, not a new inference principle.
statements.consumer: The aihuman analysis can report a finite-sample envelope for the entire sharp PSA deployment interval.
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(o\), \(N_o\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_o)\).  Exact Clopper--Pearson coverage and the union bound give
\[
\Pr_p\{p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
\geq1-\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}\frac{\alpha}{|\mathcal O|}=1-\alpha.
\]
On this event, \(p\in\mathfrak O\cap\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\).  Every \(v\) with \(Bv=p\) is feasible for the confidence optimization, so sharpness gives
\[
[L(p),U(p)]
=\{h_e^{\top}v:Bv=p,\ v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
\subseteq
\{h_e^{\top}v:Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha},\ v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
=\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Thus the asserted coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\).  Off this event an empty intersection triggers \([0,1]\), which still contains the identified set.  When the intersection is nonempty, its feasible weights form a nonempty closed subset of the compact simplex; their linear image is a compact interval and both implementation optima are attained.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the map \(x\mapsto\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x)\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\) with derivative \(\Gamma'_p\), and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\). This formula remains valid when \(p\) is on a projection face and either endpoint has multiple optimal bases.
statements.justification: The limit law exposes both sources of nonregularity instead of imposing margin conditions that remove simultaneous ties.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4, supplies the directional delta method and projection derivative; ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026, Theorem 5.1, assumes margin separation. The new formula composes the observable-polytope projection with both LP optimal-face maps for this causal identified set.
statements.consumer: It supplies pointwise standard-error simulation and diagnoses exactly when ordinary Gaussian endpoint intervals fail in finite human--AI trials.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(d=|\mathcal O|\) and \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\).  We first differentiate the projection.  Let \(t_k\downarrow0\), let \(g_k\to g\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), and set
\[
x_k=p+t_kg_k,\qquad q_k=\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(x_k),\qquad d_k=\frac{q_k-p}{t_k}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the defining minimum property of the projection gives
\[
\|q_k-x_k\|_2\leq \|p-x_k\|_2=t_k\|g_k\|_2,
\]
and hence \(\|d_k\|_2\leq2\|g_k\|_2\).  Thus \((d_k)\) is bounded.  Projection onto the nonempty closed convex polytope \(\mathfrak O\) is characterized by
\[
\langle x_k-q_k,v-q_k\rangle\leq0
\qquad(v\in\mathfrak O).
\tag{2}
\]
Every subsequential limit \(d\) of \((d_k)\) lies in \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) by the definition of that closed tangent cone.  If \(z\) is a radial tangent direction, so that \(p+t_kz\in\mathfrak O\) for all sufficiently large \(k\) after an inessential common rescaling of \(z\), substitute \(v=p+t_kz\) in (2), divide by \(t_k^2\), and pass to the relevant subsequence to obtain
\[
\langle g-d,z-d\rangle\leq0.
\tag{3}
\]
Radial directions are dense in \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\), and both sides of (3) are continuous in \(z\), so (3) holds for every \(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\).  The variational characterization of Euclidean projection onto a closed convex cone now uniquely gives
\[
d=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g.
\tag{4}
\]
Every convergent subsequence has the same limit (4), while \((d_k)\) is bounded; consequently the whole sequence converges.  This proves that \(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\), tangentially to \(\mathbb R^d\), with derivative \(g\mapsto\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  No relative-interior condition on \(p\) was used.

We next differentiate the two endpoint programs on their relative domain.  By \(\text{lem:finite-incidence-duality-continuity}\), there are finite families of affine functions
\[
\ell_r(x)=\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}x\quad(r\in R_L),
\qquad
u_s(x)=\bar\alpha_s+\bar\lambda_s^{\top}x\quad(s\in R_U)
\]
such that, on \(\mathfrak O\),
\[
L(x)=\max_{r\in R_L}\ell_r(x),
\qquad
U(x)=\min_{s\in R_U}u_s(x),
\tag{5}
\]
and every pair indexing these representations is feasible for the corresponding full dual.  Let
\[
R_L(p)=\{r:\ell_r(p)=L(p)\},
\qquad
R_U(p)=\{s:u_s(p)=U(p)\}.
\]
For \(r\notin R_L(p)\) the gap \(L(p)-\ell_r(p)\) is strictly positive, and there are only finitely many indices.  Therefore, whenever \(z_k\to z\) and \(p+t_kz_k\in\mathfrak O\), all inactive indices disappear from the maximum in (5) for sufficiently large \(k\).  It follows that
\[
\frac{L(p+t_kz_k)-L(p)}{t_k}longrightarrow
\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z.
\tag{6}
\]
The same finite-gap argument for the minimum gives
\[
\frac{U(p+t_kz_k)-U(p)}{t_k}longrightarrow
\min_{s\in R_U(p)}\bar\lambda_s^{\top}z.
\tag{7}
\]

Equations (6)--(7) equal the formulas using the entire, unnormalized optimal dual faces.  Indeed, if \((\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)\), dual feasibility implies
\[
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}(p+t_kz_k)\leq L(p+t_kz_k),
\qquad
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p=L(p).
\]
After subtraction, division by \(t_k\), and passage to the limit, (6) yields
\[
\lambda^{\top}z\leq\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z.
\tag{8}
\]
Conversely, each active pair from (5) belongs to \(\Lambda_L(p)\), so equality holds after maximizing (8) over the full face.  Thus
\[
L'_p(z)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z.
\tag{9}
\]
The analogous inequalities, with their directions reversed, give
\[
U'_p(z)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z.
\tag{10}
\]
Although the dual pairs are unnormalized, (9)--(10) are gauge safe: every \(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) satisfies \(\mathbf 1^{\top}z=0\), since \(\mathfrak O\) lies in the probability simplex, and the transformation \((\alpha,\lambda)\mapsto(\alpha-c,\lambda+c\mathbf1)\) does not change \(\lambda^{\top}z\).

For the sequence in (1), equation (4) says \((q_k-p)/t_k\to z:=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Apply (6)--(10) with \(q_k=p+t_kd_k\).  We obtain
\[
\frac{\Phi(p+t_kg_k)-\Phi(p)}{t_k}longrightarrow
\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right)
=\Gamma'_p(g).
\tag{11}
\]
This is Hadamard directional differentiability.  The derivative is continuous because it is the composition of the continuous projection onto a closed convex cone with a finite piecewise-linear endpoint map.  Multiple active facets, and hence multiple optimal LP bases, are retained in the maximum and minimum in (11).

Under \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\), \(\text{lem:finite-multinomial-clt}\) gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\rightsquigarrow G_p.
\tag{12}
\]
The estimator in \(\text{def:projection-endpoint-estimator}\) satisfies \(\widehat\theta=\Phi(\widehat p)\) and \(\Phi(p)=\theta(p)\), because \(p\in\mathfrak O\).  Apply \(\text{lem:hadamard-directional-delta-method}\) to (11)--(12).  This yields
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p),
\]
including when \(p\) is on a projection face and either optimal dual face is non-singleton.

statements.statement: If there is \(j^{\star}\in J_0\) with \(c_e(s)=c_{j^{\star}}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^{\star}]\). Separately, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then \(Z\) is fully observed, but full revelation alone does not point-identify every distinct untrialed configuration: there exist two legal SCMs with the same fully labeled trial law and different untrialed means. Identification may nevertheless occur at special observed laws, through configuration overlap, through the neutral-invariance restriction, or under further identifying restrictions.
statements.justification: The sanity check recovers ordinary randomized identification exactly under configuration equality and keeps full revelation logically separate from policy overlap.
statements.gap: ImaiJiangGreinerHalenShin2023 identifies observed randomized recommendation arms; the reduction embeds precisely that case and makes no universal identification claim for a distinct untrialed configuration.
statements.consumer: Implementations can test the standard RCT case without falsely declaring identification merely because all labels are revealed.
statements.proof_tex:
If \(c_e(s)=c_{j^\star}(s)\) for every \(s\), then \(h_e(t)=y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)\).  Since \(\rho_{j^\star}>0\), randomization and the common outcome response give, for every compatible \(v\),
\[
\mathbb E_v[Y\mid D=j^\star]
=\rho_{j^\star}^{-1}\sum_tv_t\rho_{j^\star}y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)
=h_e^{\top}v.
\]
The left side is fixed by \(p\), so every \(v\) in the fiber has that target.  Sharpness gives \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^\star]\).

If \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\), then \(R=1\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) almost surely.  Nevertheless full revelation alone need not identify a distinct configuration.  Take one stratum, a trialed configuration \((1,q_\ell)\), an untrialed configuration \((1,q_h)\), and \(q_\ell<q_h\).  In two deterministic SCMs set \(Z=1\), all actions to one, and all neutral outcomes to zero.  Set
\[
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,0)
\quad\text{in the first model},\qquad
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,1)
\quad\text{in the second}.
\]
Both types satisfy correctness, neutrality, and both performance orders.  Their fully labeled trial laws coincide, but their untrialed means are zero and one.  This proves that revelation alone is insufficient while leaving intact the stated special-law, overlap, neutral-invariance, and further-restriction exceptions.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\), put \(\beta=1-\alpha\), write \((D_L,D_U)=\Gamma'_p\), and define \(H(g)=\max\{D_L(g),-D_U(g)\}\).  Let
\[
V_p=\{g:\mathbf 1^{\top}g=0,\ g_o=0\text{ whenever }p_o=0\}.
\]
Suppose the active projection cones and extreme slopes of \(\Lambda_L(p)\) and \(\Lambda_U(p)\), refined by their zero and comparison hyperplanes, yield a finite polyhedral fan on \(V_p\) such that: (i) locally,
\[
\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(p+x))-\theta(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x)),
\]
with both coordinates linear on each fan cone; and (ii) every facet normal is nonzero on \(V_p\).  Let \(\mathcal A_p\) be the finite closure under row selection and sign changes of matrices whose rows are the restrictions to \(V_p\) of the fan facet normals and endpoint slopes that are nonzero on \(V_p\).  With \(\mathbf e_o\) denoting the standard basis vector of observable cell \(o\), define
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p),
\]
from an independent size-\(m\) categorical sample, define
\[
\delta_m(p)=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_p}\sup_x
\left|\Pr_p\{AX_m\leq x\}-\Pr\{AG_p\leq x\}\right|.
\]
Assume Gaussian nondegeneracy on \(V_p\), meaning
\[
v^{\top}\Sigma_pv>0\quad\text{for every nonzero }v\in V_p,
\]
and assume
\[
m_n\to\infty,\qquad m_n^2/n\to0,\qquad\eta_n\downarrow0,
\]
and
\[
\frac{\delta_{m_n}(p)+m_n/\sqrt n+m_n^2/n}{\eta_n}\to0.
\]
Then \(\delta_m(p)\to0\), atoms of \(H(G_p)\) can occur only at zero, and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\left\{
L(p)\geq\widehat L-\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n},\
U(p)\leq\widehat U+\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n}
\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
No projection-cone or LP-basis uniqueness, and no further restriction on fan cones where \(H\) vanishes, is required.  The fan, the exact multinomial probabilities defining \(\delta_m(p)\), and the Gaussian orthant probabilities are finite and enumerable.

For the thirty-two-type table the conditions are nonvacuous.  In its stated row order, let
\[
p_\star=B^{32}_{\cdot,1}=B^{32}_{\cdot,17}
=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_7).
\]
This is a boundary vertex of \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), and every mixture of types \(1\) and \(17\) is optimal for both endpoint programs.  If \(\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1/4)\), then \(G_{p_\star}=\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\), and exact active-cone enumeration gives
\[
D_L(G_{p_\star})=0,\qquad
D_U(G_{p_\star})=\frac45|\zeta|,\qquad
H(G_{p_\star})=0.
\]
Thus the exact Gaussian directional law is the unit atom at zero, and the asserted conservative conclusion holds for every \(m_n\to\infty\) with \(m_n^2/n\to0\) and every decreasing slack satisfying the displayed dominance condition.
statements.justification: Finite active-cone geometry, global sign preservation, and a slack-dominating multinomial approximation rate make centered subsampling conservative at the only possible atom, zero, without any restriction on zero regions of the fan.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 supplies the directional delta method but not atom-valid centered subsampling; this theorem gives a finite, enumerable, pointwise certificate for the projection-composed endpoint pair without unique projection cones, unique LP bases, or an additional zero-region condition.
statements.consumer: The boundary implementation can certify a subsample and slack schedule for simultaneous endpoint reporting at projection and LP ties, subject to the stated pointwise rate and fan conditions.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(d=|\mathcal O|\), let \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\), and define
\[
X_n=\sqrt n(\widehat p-p),
\qquad
T_n=\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat L-L(p)),\sqrt n(U(p)-\widehat U)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{lem:finite-multinomial-clt}\), whose sampling premise is \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\),
\[
X_n\rightsquigarrow G_p,
\qquad X_n=O_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, \(X_n\in V_p\) almost surely: its coordinates sum to zero, and \(p_o=0\) implies \(N_o=0\) almost surely.  Assumption (i) in the theorem supplies \(r>0\) such that
\[
\Phi(p+x)-\Phi(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x))
\quad\text{for }x\in V_p, \|x\|_2<r.
\tag{3}
\]
The two directional coordinates are continuous, positively homogeneous, and linear on each cone of a finite fan.  Compactness of the unit sphere in \(V_p\), or simply finiteness of its slopes, therefore gives a constant \(C_D<\infty\) for which
\[
|D_L(x)|\vee|D_U(x)|\leq C_D\|x\|_2
\qquad(x\in V_p).
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) and positive homogeneity imply
\[
T_n=H(X_n)
\tag{5}
\]
with probability tending to one.  Since \(H\) is continuous, (2) also gives \(H(X_n)\rightsquigarrow H(G_p)\).

We compare the conditional subsampling law to an independent size-\(m\) experiment, where below \(m=m_n\).  Let \(\Pr^*\) denote probability conditional on the full sample, let \(\widehat p_b\) be the empirical law of a uniformly selected size-\(m\) subsample without replacement, and put
\[
a_n=\sqrt m(\widehat p-p)=\sqrt{m/n}\,X_n.
\tag{6}
\]
On the event that both empirical laws are in the neighborhood in (3), the centered statistic defining the conditional critical value is exactly
\[
S_{n,b}=max\left\{
D_L\bigl(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)\bigr)-D_L(a_n),
D_U(a_n)-D_U\bigl(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)\bigr)
\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
This follows by applying (3) at \(\widehat p_b\) and \(\widehat p\), subtracting, multiplying by \(\sqrt m\), and using positive homogeneity.

Couple the ordered indices sampled without replacement to \(m\) independent indices sampled with replacement from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  A coupling failure requires a repeated with-replacement index, so the union bound gives conditional failure probability at most
\[
\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}.
\tag{8}
\]
For each with-replacement draw, maximally couple its empirical categorical law \(\widehat p\) to the population law \(p\).  The mismatch probability for one draw is
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\widehat p,p)=\frac12\|\widehat p-p\|_1.
\]
Another union bound shows that all \(m\) categories agree except on an event of conditional probability at most
\[
\frac m2\|\widehat p-p\|_1.
\tag{9}
\]
On \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), (9) is bounded by \(m\sqrt d M/(2\sqrt n)\).

Let
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p)
\]
be formed from an independent size-\(m\) sample with law \(p\).  On the successful coupling event, \(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)=X_m\), and the comparison variable in (7) becomes
\[
K_{a_n}(X_m),
\qquad
K_a(g):=\max\{D_L(g)-D_L(a),D_U(a)-D_U(g)\}.
\tag{10}
\]

We also control failure of the local representation (3).  Each coordinate of \(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p\) is centered and lies in \([-1,1]\).  For all sufficiently small \(|u|\), Taylor's formula on this bounded interval gives a constant \(C_1\), depending only on the finite alphabet, such that
\[
\mathbb E_p\exp\{u(\mathbf1\{O_i=o\}-p_o)\}\leq\exp(C_1u^2).
\]
Independence, exponential Markov inequality, optimization over \(u\), and a union bound over the \(d\) coordinates give constants \(C_2,c_2>0\) such that
\[
\Pr_p\{\|X_m\|_2>r\sqrt m/2\}\leq C_2e^{-c_2m}.
\tag{11}
\]
For fixed \(M\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\|X_n\|_2\leq M\) puts \(\widehat p\) in the radius-\(r/2\) neighborhood in (3).  Equations (8)--(11) therefore bound the conditional total-variation error between \(S_{n,b}\) and \(K_{a_n}(X_m)\), on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), by
\[
q_{n,M}:=\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}+\frac{m\sqrt d M}{2\sqrt n}+C_2e^{-c_2m}.
\tag{12}
\]

We next verify that the explicitly defined multinomial approximation error vanishes.  For every \(A\in\mathcal A_p\), the finite multinomial central limit theorem gives
\[
AX_m\rightsquigarrow AG_p.
\tag{13}
\]
Delete identically zero rows of \(A\).  By condition (ii) and the construction of \(\mathcal A_p\), each remaining row is nonzero on \(V_p\).  Gaussian nondegeneracy on \(V_p\) makes each corresponding marginal of \(AG_p\) non-atomic.  The boundary of every lower orthant is contained in a finite union of coordinate hyperplanes, and hence has \(AG_p\)-probability zero.  Thus (13) gives pointwise convergence of all lower-orthant probabilities.  A finite grid on a sufficiently large compact box, coordinatewise monotonicity between grid points, and tightness outside the box upgrade this convergence to uniform convergence over lower orthants.  Since \(\mathcal A_p\) is finite,
\[
\delta_m(p)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{14}
\]

On each pair of fan cones containing \(a_n\) and \(g\), the event \(K_{a_n}(g)\leq x\) is an intersection of linear inequalities.  The normals are selected endpoint slopes, fan-facet normals, and their sign changes.  Taking the finite union over cone pairs, and using the stipulated closure properties of \(\mathcal A_p\), writes this event as a finite Boolean combination of lower orthants governed by matrices in \(\mathcal A_p\).  Inclusion--exclusion therefore bounds the difference between its probability under \(X_m\) and under \(G_p\) by \(C_F\delta_m(p)\), for a finite constant \(C_F\) depending only on the fixed fan.  In addition, (4) gives the deterministic, uniform bound
\[
|K_{a_n}(g)-H(g)|
\leq |D_L(a_n)|\vee|D_U(a_n)|
\leq C_D\|a_n\|_2.
\tag{15}
\]
On \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), equations (6), (12), (14), and (15), together with \(m^2/n\to0\), imply, at every continuity point \(x\) of the distribution of \(H(G_p)\),
\[
\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}\leq x\}\longrightarrow
\Pr\{H(G_p)\leq x\}
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{16}
\]
Because \(X_n=O_{\Pr}(1)\), we remove the restriction to bounded \(X_n\) by letting \(M\to\infty\).

Let \(F(x)=\Pr\{H(G_p)\leq x\}\).  On the interior of each full-dimensional cone of the fan refined by the endpoint-comparison and zero hyperplanes, \(H\) is one homogeneous linear functional.  Proper cone boundaries lie in finitely many hyperplanes whose normals are nonzero on \(V_p\), and therefore have Gaussian probability zero.  A nonzero linear functional of \(G_p\) has a continuous Gaussian law, whereas a zero linear functional is identically zero.  It follows that
\[
F\text{ can have an atom only at }0.
\tag{17}
\]

Put \(\beta=1-\alpha\), let \(c_n=c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,\beta+\eta_n}\), with the lower-quantile convention \(\inf\{x:\Pr^*(S_{n,b}\leq x)\geq\beta+\eta_n\}\), and define \(q_\beta=\inf\{x:F(x)\geq\beta\}\).  Suppose first that \(q_\beta\neq0\).  For every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), \(x_\varepsilon=q_\beta-\varepsilon\) is a continuity point and satisfies \(F(x_\varepsilon)<\beta\).  Equation (16) and \(\eta_n\to0\) imply \(\Pr\{c_n>x_\varepsilon\}\to1\).  Equations (5), (17), and weak convergence then yield
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq F(x_\varepsilon).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and using the absence of an atom at the nonzero point \(q_\beta\), gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq F(q_\beta)\geq\beta.
\tag{18}
\]

It remains to handle \(q_\beta=0\), when
\[
F(0-)\leq\beta\leq F(0).
\tag{19}
\]
Fix a realization \(z=X_n\) satisfying \(H(z)=0\).  Since \(H(z)=\max\{D_L(z),-D_U(z)\}=0\), positive homogeneity and (6) give
\[
D_L(a_n)=\sqrt{m/n}\,D_L(z)\leq0,
\qquad
D_U(a_n)=\sqrt{m/n}\,D_U(z)\geq0.
\tag{20}
\]
For every \(g\in V_p\), these inequalities imply the global sign preservation
\[
\begin{aligned}
K_{a_n}(g)<0
&\Longrightarrow D_L(g)<D_L(a_n)\leq0
\ \text{and}\ D_U(g)>D_U(a_n)\geq0\\
&\Longrightarrow H(g)<0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
\]
This step uses neither a selected projection cone nor a unique endpoint slope.

The event \(\{H(g)<0\}\) is a finite union of intersections of strict linear inequalities from the refined fan.  Approximate strict thresholds from below and apply the same finite inclusion--exclusion comparison used above.  It gives
\[
\Pr_p\{H(X_m)<0\}\leq F(0-)+C_F\delta_m(p).
\tag{22}
\]
Combining (12), (21), and (22), uniformly on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M,H(X_n)=0\}\), yields
\[
\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}<0\}
\leq F(0-)+C_F\delta_m(p)
+\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}+\frac{m\sqrt d M}{2\sqrt n}+C_2e^{-c_2m}.
\tag{23}
\]

If \(F(0-)=\beta\), then \(\beta>0\) and \(H(G_p)<0\) with positive probability.  Hence at least one endpoint slope \(\ell\), nonzero on \(V_p\), occurs as a row of a matrix in \(\mathcal A_p\).  The scalar \(\ell^{\top}X_m\) has at most \((m+1)^d\) support points, so one of its jumps has size at least \((m+1)^{-d}\).  The law of \(\ell^{\top}G_p\) is continuous by nondegeneracy.  Comparing the two distribution functions immediately before and at that jump proves
\[
\delta_m(p)\geq\frac{1}{2(m+1)^d}.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus \(e^{-c_2m}=o(\delta_m(p))\).  Define
\[
R_n=\delta_{m_n}(p)+\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{m_n^2}{n}.
\]
The assumed rate condition is \(R_n=o(\eta_n)\).  If \(F(0-)=\beta\), equations (23)--(24) make its right-hand side \(\beta+o_{\Pr}(\eta_n)\); if \(F(0-)<\beta\), equations (14) and (23) instead leave a fixed positive gap below \(\beta\).  A lower \((\beta+\eta_n)\)-quantile of a finite distribution is nonnegative whenever the mass strictly below zero is less than \(\beta+\eta_n\).  Since \(X_n=O_{\Pr}(1)\), we conclude that
\[
\Pr\{H(X_n)=0,\ c_n<0\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]

We also have \(c_n=o_{\Pr}(1)\).  For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(q_\beta=0\) implies \(F(-\varepsilon)<\beta\), so (16) gives \(c_n>-\varepsilon\) with probability tending to one.  Also \(F(\varepsilon)>\beta\): this is immediate if \(F(0)>\beta\); if \(F(0)=\beta\) and \(H\) takes a positive value, continuity, positive homogeneity, and full Gaussian support on \(V_p\) give a positive-probability open set on which \(0<H(G_p)\leq\varepsilon\); if \(H\) never takes a positive value, then \(F(\varepsilon)=1\).  Another application of (16) gives \(c_n\leq\varepsilon\) with probability tending to one.  Hence
\[
c_n=o_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{26}
\]

The zero set \(Z_H=\{g\in V_p:H(g)=0\}\) is a finite union of interiors of full-dimensional fan cones on which the selected linear functional is zero, together with subsets of finitely many zero and fan-facet hyperplanes.  Its boundary is therefore contained in finitely many hyperplanes with normals nonzero on \(V_p\).  Gaussian nondegeneracy gives \(\Pr\{G_p\in\partial Z_H\}=0\).  Thus \(Z_H\) is a continuity set for the weak convergence in (2), and
\[
\Pr\{H(X_n)=0\}\longrightarrow
\Pr\{H(G_p)=0\}=F(0)-F(0-).
\tag{27}
\]
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), equations (5), (25), and (26) ensure, up to an event of probability tending to zero, coverage of both disjoint events \(\{H(X_n)\leq-\varepsilon\}\) and \(\{H(X_n)=0\}\).  Equations (17) and (27) therefore imply
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}
\geq F(-\varepsilon)+F(0)-F(0-).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) makes the right-hand side \(F(0)\geq\beta\) by (19).  Together with (18), this proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]
By (1), the event in (28) is precisely
\[
\left\{L(p)\geq\widehat L-c_n/\sqrt n,\quad
U(p)\leq\widehat U+c_n/\sqrt n\right\}.
\]
Because \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) and \(\alpha>0\), the level \(1-\alpha+\eta_n\) lies in \((0,1)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), which is enough for the limiting assertion.

It remains to verify the stated thirty-two-type boundary certificate.  By \(\text{thm:complete-32-type-refinement-certificate}\), the table in \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) is the complete observable--target quotient.  Every column of \(B^{32}\) has one entry \(1/2\) in each trial-arm block.  If a convex combination of columns equals
\[
p_\star=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_7),
\]
every positively weighted column must be supported on rows \(1\) and \(7\), by nonnegativity.  Inspection of the complete table shows that precisely columns \(1\) and \(17\) have this support, that the two columns coincide, and that \(h^{32}_1=h^{32}_{17}=0\).  Hence \(p_\star\) is a vertex, its fiber is the segment joining types \(1\) and \(17\), and every point on that segment is optimal for both endpoint programs with value zero.  The multinomial covariance on the two positive cells gives
\[
G_{p_\star}=\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7),
\qquad \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1/4).
\tag{29}
\]

We enumerate the projection on the two rays of \(V_{p_\star}=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7\}\).  First suppose \(\zeta>0\), divide all candidate tangent coordinates by \(\zeta\), and consider mass leaving high-arm row \(7\).  Four outgoing high-arm cells, rows \(8,9,10,12\), are reachable while retaining low-arm row \(1\).  Let \(r\geq0\) be their total outgoing coordinate.  The remaining outgoing high-arm row \(11\), with coordinate \(t\geq0\), can only be reached by columns that also leave low-arm row \(1\) for row \(2\) or row \(5\).  Consequently the low-arm contribution to squared distance from \(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7\) is at least
\[
(1+t)^2+t^2/2,
\tag{30}
\]
where the second term is the minimum squared norm obtained by splitting total mass \(t\) between two cells.  Splitting \(r\) among its four high-arm cells similarly shows that the high-arm contribution is at least
\[
(1-r-t)^2+r^2/4+t^2.
\tag{31}
\]
The sum of (30)--(31) is convex on \(r,t\geq0\), and its derivative with respect to \(t\) is \(2r+7t\).  Its minimum therefore has \(t=0\).  Minimization in \(r\) then gives \(r=4/5\), equally divided among the four reachable cells.  This lower bound is attained by the displayed table columns, proving
\[
\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)}
\{\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\}
=\frac{\zeta}{5}(-4\mathbf e_7+\mathbf e_8+\mathbf e_9+\mathbf e_{10}+\mathbf e_{12}).
\tag{32}
\]
For \(\zeta<0\), the arm-swapped enumeration uses low-arm outgoing rows \(2,3,4,5\) and gives
\[
\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)}
\{\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\}
=\frac{|\zeta|}{5}(-4\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3+\mathbf e_4+\mathbf e_5).
\tag{33}
\]

On either ray, each of the four outgoing cells has a target-zero representative, and all target coordinates are nonnegative.  Hence
\[
D_L(G_{p_\star})=0.
\tag{34}
\]
Exactly two outgoing cells on each ray have target-one representatives whose other observed cell is the relevant base cell.  An incidence entry is \(1/2\), so producing outgoing observable derivative \(|\zeta|/5\) requires type-weight derivative \(2|\zeta|/5\).  Assigning each of the two eligible cells to its target-one representative attains total target derivative \(4|\zeta|/5\).  Conversely, nonnegative weights on nonbase columns cannot cancel an outgoing observable coordinate.  Thus only columns supported on a base cell and one of the four displayed outgoing cells can enter a tangent representation of (32) or (33), and table completeness shows that only the same two cells have a target-one such column.  This proves the matching upper bound and therefore
\[
D_U(G_{p_\star})=\frac45|\zeta|,
\qquad H(G_{p_\star})=0.
\tag{35}
\]

Because \(\mathfrak O^{32}\) is a polytope, a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(p_\star\) agrees with the corresponding neighborhood of \(p_\star+T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)\): in a finite inequality representation, active inequalities define the tangent cone and inactive inequalities retain positive slack.  If \(y=\Pi_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star+x)\), projection optimality against \(p_\star\) gives
\[
\|y-p_\star\|_2^2\leq x^{\top}(y-p_\star)
\leq\|x\|_2\|y-p_\star\|_2,
\]
and hence \(\|y-p_\star\|_2\leq\|x\|_2\).  Small inputs therefore project inside that common neighborhood, making (32)--(33) exact local formulas.  The target-zero and target-one allocations proving (34)--(35) remain feasible with weights linear in \(|\zeta|\), and the nonnegativity argument gives the matching local upper bounds.  The two rays form a finite fan; after vacuous whole-space equalities are discarded, its proper facet normals are nonzero on the one-dimensional space \(V_{p_\star}\).  Equation (29) is nondegenerate on that space.  Thus conditions (i)--(ii) hold even though both endpoint fibers have multiple optima, and (35) proves that the exact Gaussian directional law of \(H\) is the unit atom at zero.

Finally, (14) and \(m_n^2/n\to0\) imply
\[
r_n:=\delta_{m_n}(p_\star)+m_n/\sqrt n+m_n^2/n\longrightarrow0.
\]
The positive nonincreasing sequence
\[
\eta_n^\star=\sup_{k\geq n}\sqrt{r_k}+n^{-1}
\]
satisfies \(\eta_n^\star\downarrow0\) and
\[
0\leq\frac{r_n}{\eta_n^\star}\leq\sqrt{r_n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Hence admissible slack schedules exist, and every decreasing schedule satisfying the theorem's displayed dominance condition yields the asserted pointwise conservative coverage.

statements.statement:
Let \(B\) have finitely many columns \(b_t\), let \(h_e(t)\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathfrak O=B\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  The lower and upper programs attain their optima.  Moreover,
\[
L(p)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\qquad
U(p)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\]
and both optimal faces are nonempty for every \(p\in\mathfrak O\).  The four value functions obtained from \(B\) and \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) are finite piecewise-affine functions, continuous on their entire relative domains.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(b_t=B_{\cdot,t}\), \(h_t=h_e(t)\), and form the finite observable--target hull
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{(Bv,h_e^{\top}v):v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\right\}
=\operatorname{conv}\{(b_t,h_t):t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The simplex is compact and the maps in (1) are linear.  Hence \(\mathcal C\), every fiber \(\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\}\), and its image under \(v\mapsto h_e^{\top}v\) are compact.  For \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the last image is a nonempty compact interval, because the fiber is convex.  Its endpoints are therefore attained and equal \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\) by \(\text{def:sharp-endpoint-programs}\).

We derive a finite half-space representation rather than assuming a normalization of a dual variable.  The membership condition \((x,z)\in\mathcal C\) is the finite linear system
\[
v_t\geq0\ (t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}),\qquad
\mathbf 1^{\top}v=1,\qquad Bv=x,\qquad h_e^{\top}v=z.
\tag{2}
\]
Eliminate the coordinates of \(v\) successively.  At one elimination step, inequalities with positive coefficient of the eliminated coordinate give upper bounds, inequalities with negative coefficient give lower bounds, and inequalities with zero coefficient are retained; existence of that coordinate is equivalent to every retained lower bound being no larger than every retained upper bound.  Thus one step replaces a finite system by a finite system and is an equivalence.  Induction over the finitely many coordinates in (2) gives finite sets \(R\), vectors \(a_r\), and scalars \(d_r,c_r\) such that
\[
\mathcal C=\{(x,z):a_r^{\top}x+d_rz\leq c_r\text{ for every }r\in R\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The valid inequalities \(-z\leq0\) and \(z\leq1\), which follow from \(h_t\in\{0,1\}\), may be appended to (3).  Hence the index sets \(R_-:=\{r:d_r<0\}\) and \(R_+:=\{r:d_r>0\}\) are nonempty.

For fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the inequalities with \(d_r=0\) are already satisfied, and (3) says exactly
\[
L(p)=\max_{r\in R_-}\frac{c_r-a_r^{\top}p}{d_r},
\qquad
U(p)=\min_{r\in R_+}\frac{c_r-a_r^{\top}p}{d_r}.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(r\in R_-\), write the affine function in (4) as \(\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}p\).  Substitution of each generator \((b_t,h_t)\) into its defining inequality gives
\[
\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}b_t\leq h_t\quad\text{for every }t,
\tag{5}
\]
so \((\alpha_r,\lambda_r)\in\mathcal D_L\).  Conversely, if \((\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L\) and \(Bv=p\), \(\mathbf 1^{\top}v=1\), then
\[
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p
=\sum_t v_t(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}b_t)
\leq\sum_t v_th_t=h_e^{\top}v.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking the minimum in (6), then choosing an index attaining the finite maximum in (4), proves
\[
L(p)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}
(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p),
\tag{7}
\]
with a nonempty optimal face.  The same argument with \(r\in R_+\) reverses (5)--(6) and proves
\[
U(p)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}
(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p),
\tag{8}
\]
again with attainment.

Equation (4) represents \(L\) as the maximum of finitely many affine functions and \(U\) as the minimum of finitely many affine functions.  They are therefore finite, piecewise affine, and continuous at every point of \(\mathfrak O\), including its relative boundary.  Repeating (1)--(8) with the finite matrix \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) proves the corresponding assertions for \(L_{\mathrm{blind}}\) and \(U_{\mathrm{blind}}\) on \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\mathfrak O\).

statements.statement:
For every finite selective-label incidence model and every \(p\in\mathfrak O\),
\[
L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing,
\]
and
\[
U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, the lower inequality is strict exactly when the linear system
\[
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\leq h_e,\qquad
\lambda=K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu,\qquad
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p=L(p)
\]
is infeasible, and the upper inequality is strict exactly when the system obtained by replacing \(\leq,L\) with \(\geq,U\) is infeasible.  Consequently \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\) is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\).  If \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) holds, then \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\cap\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\) is nonempty and contains a nonempty relatively open subset of \(\mathfrak O\).  A law supported on the bracket stratum has both full-versus-blind gaps equal to \(199/800\); mixing it by a sufficiently small positive amount with any law assigning positive mass to every legal response type gives the asserted relative-interior region.  Duplicate low- or high-performance arms, arbitrary positive randomization probabilities, additional performance values, other strata, and configurations away from the bracket stratum do not invalidate this construction.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\).  By \(\text{lem:finite-incidence-duality-continuity}\), the full lower dual optimum is attained on \(\Lambda_L(p)\), and the blind lower dual is
\[
\max_{\alpha,\mu}\left\{\alpha+\mu^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}p:
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\leq h_e\right\}.
\tag{37}
\]
Under the substitution \(\lambda=K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\), its feasible set is exactly \(\mathcal D_L\cap\mathcal E_K\), and its objective is \(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\).  Thus (37) is the maximum of the full lower-dual objective over the embedded blind subset.  Attainment of both finite programs gives
\[
L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)=L(p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K\neq\varnothing.
\tag{38}
\]
By \(\text{lem:z-blind-coarsening}\), the blind lower endpoint is no larger than the full lower endpoint.  Negating equality in this ordered pair proves
\[
L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\tag{39}
\]

Likewise, the blind upper dual is
\[
\min_{\alpha,\mu}\left\{\alpha+\mu^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}p:
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\geq h_e\right\},
\tag{40}
\]
the restriction of the full upper dual to \(\mathcal D_U\cap\mathcal E_K\).  Hence
\[
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)=U(p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K\neq\varnothing.
\tag{41}
\]
The upper inclusion from \(\text{lem:z-blind-coarsening}\) then gives
\[
U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\tag{42}
\]
Equations (38)--(42) also prove the advertised computable tests: after the finite primal programs produce \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\), every displayed condition is a finite linear equality or inequality in \((\alpha,\lambda,\mu)\).

By \(\text{lem:finite-incidence-duality-continuity}\), the four endpoint functions are continuous on their relative domains.  Since \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) is linear, the gap functions
\[
g_L(p)=L(p)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),
\qquad
g_U(p)=U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)-U(p)
\tag{43}
\]
are continuous on \(\mathfrak O\).  Therefore
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}
=g_L^{-1}((0,\infty))\cap g_U^{-1}((0,\infty))
\tag{44}
\]
is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\), including at relative-boundary laws.

It remains to establish nonemptiness under \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Fix \(s_*\in\mathcal S\) and \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\) supplied by \(\text{def:bracket-stratum-design}\).  Extend each row of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) to every additional performance value as follows.  If \(z=0\), set the neutral outcome to one for every \(q\) and extend its nonincreasing \(r=1\) path by
\[
Y_{(1,q)}=
\begin{cases}
Y_{(1,q_\ell)},&q<q_m,\\
Y_{(1,q_m)},&q=q_m,\\
Y_{(1,q_h)},&q>q_m.
\end{cases}
\tag{45}
\]
If \(z=1\), set the neutral outcome to zero for every \(q\) and use (45) for the nondecreasing \(r=1\) path.  Formula (45) agrees at the three distinguished values, is monotone in the required direction, and stays below the neutral value when \(z=0\) and above it when \(z=1\).  Thus correctness, both performance orders, and neutral invariance hold at every additional \(q\).

Retain the two endpoint action bits.  Fix arbitrarily, say at zero, every action coordinate not read by the trial incidence map at \(s_*\).  This explicitly includes \(A_{(1,q_m)}\): deployment uses it under \(e\), but \(e\notin J_0\), so no randomized trial row reads it, and the target \(h_e\) reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\).  It also includes action coordinates at all other nontrialed configurations.  The legal-type definition places no cross-coordinate restriction on these actions, so the extension remains legal.  This constructs legal general-design extensions of all thirty-two displayed rows.

Conversely, restriction of any legal response type with \(S=s_*\) to \(q_\ell,q_m,q_h\) has one of the four binary monotone three-point paths covered by \(\text{thm:complete-32-type-refinement-certificate}\), after replacing the unread neutral constant by its canonical displayed representative when necessary.  Its endpoint action pair is one of the four binary pairs; all action coordinates not read by the trial incidence map, including \(A_{(1,q_m)}\), may be fixed without changing the trial law or the outcome-only target.  By that theorem's complete quotient-generating cover, it therefore shares its trial-observable column and middle target with a displayed representative.  Additional performance values and off-stratum configurations do not create new observable--target columns in a law supported on \(s_*\).

Put weights \(w^{32}(\pi^{32,\circ})\) on fixed legal extensions of the thirty-two rows and zero mass outside \(s_*\), and call the resulting vector \(w_0\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  A trial arm \(j\) using endpoint \(d\in\{\ell,h\}\) contributes \(\rho_j\) times its conditional-cell indicator, while the canonical table contributes one half of that indicator.  Thus its expanded block is the canonical endpoint block multiplied by \(2\rho_j>0\).  Because the bracket condition supplies at least one arm of each endpoint kind and every \(\rho_j>0\), selecting one block of each kind and dividing by \(2\rho_j\) is a left inverse.  Consequently, equality of expanded full laws is equivalent to equality of their canonical full laws; the same statement holds after the revealed-label cells are summed by the blind map.  Moreover, an expanded law having zero probability outside \(s_*\) cannot be generated by any positive weight on a response type with a different stratum, because every trial arm has positive probability.  Hence other strata and duplicated or rescaled endpoint arms enlarge neither relevant fiber.

The four endpoint programs at the constructed law are therefore the canonical programs at \(p^{32,\circ}\), after quotienting duplicate columns.  The complete certificate gives
\[
L-L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\frac{397-198}{800}=\frac{199}{800},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}-U=1-\frac{601}{800}=\frac{199}{800}.
\tag{46}
\]
Set \(p_0=Bw_0\).  Equation (46) proves \(p_0\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\) without a restriction on other strata or on configurations away from \(s_*\).

Because \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) is finite and nonempty, choose \(u\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) with \(u_t>0\) for every legal response type.  For \(0<\delta<1\), let
\[
w_\delta=(1-\delta)w_0+\delta u,
\qquad
p_\delta=Bw_\delta.
\tag{47}
\]
Every coordinate of \(w_\delta\) is positive.  Aggregate weights of duplicate columns and enumerate the distinct generators of \(\mathfrak O\) as \(b_1,\ldots,b_N\), obtaining aggregate weights \(\beta_k>0\).  On the zero-sum coefficient space, the linear map \(T(x)=\sum_kx_kb_k\) surjects onto the direction space \(V=\operatorname{span}\{b_k-b_1:2\leq k\leq N\}\).  Choose a linear right inverse \(R:V\to\{x:\mathbf 1^{\top}x=0\}\).  When \(V\neq\{0\}\), let \(C=\sup_{\|d\|_2=1}\|Rd\|_\infty<\infty\).  For every \(d\in V\) with \(\|d\|_2<\min_k\beta_k/C\), the weights \(\beta+Rd\) are nonnegative, sum to one, and generate \(p_\delta+d\).  The case \(V=\{0\}\) is immediate.  This relative neighborhood proves \(p_\delta\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\).  By continuity in (43), the two gaps remain positive for every sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), since both equal \(199/800\) at \(\delta=0\).  Thus
\[
p_\delta\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\cap\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O).
\tag{48}
\]
By the definition of relative interior as interior in the affine hull, \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\) is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\).  Hence (44) shows that \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\cap\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\) is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\), and (48) shows that it is nonempty.  The block-rescaling and extension arguments above also establish the claimed robustness to duplicate endpoint arms, arbitrary positive randomization probabilities, extra performance values, other strata, and off-stratum configurations.

sampling_model.design: Each unit is assigned independently to a trialed policy \(D\in J_0\) with known probability \(\rho_j>0\); the untrialed policy \(e\) is never assigned.
sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_i=(D_i,S_i,A_i,Y_i,Z_{\mathrm{obs},i})\) are independent draws from a finite population law induced by one common response-type mixture \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is the randomized policy index. Policy \(j\) supplies the known recommendation--performance configuration \(c_j(S)\), which elicits action \(A_{c_j(S)}\) and downstream outcome \(Y_{c_j(S)}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every trialed arm has known strictly positive probability \(\rho_j\). No overlap is imposed for \(e\), because its mean is partially identified through structural response restrictions rather than observed assignments.
sampling_model.label_observation: Ground truth \(Z\) is recorded exactly when the endogenous action has \(A=1\); otherwise the recorded label is \(\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The only estimated nuisance is the finite multinomial observable law \(p\). Certified performance values and policy configuration maps are treated as external design inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 gives valid conditional-mean bounds under counterfactual correctness, performance order, neutrality, and bounded outcomes, while its tightness discussion does not claim sharpness and Appendix G treats a restricted missing-label mechanism; it does not give the present dual-face criterion for the value of revealed labels.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 give attained tight bounds in a performance-mediated model without the selective-label correctness quotient or a full-versus-label-blind optimal-face characterization.
Proposition 4.1 studies decision-induced labels through contraction across decision makers, not the sharp compatible-SCM fiber or the two-sided value of retaining revealed labels.

Theorem 3 and Theorem S3 give sharp classification-risk contrasts under a randomized single-blinded evaluation design, rather than downstream policy means under the present SLCC response restrictions and endogenous revelation.

Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 provide generic finite response-function optimization, and Section 6 with Appendix E propagates observable-law confidence regions; they do not provide the mass-aware full-versus-coarsened dual-face equivalence or the primitive bracket-stratum nonemptiness construction.

The paper derives tight symbolic bounds for discrete causal effects by polynomial-program methods, but does not characterize when a specified label-revelation coarsening strictly changes both endpoint faces or give the SLCC bracket family.

The paper studies counterfactual risk assessment under unmeasured confounding, whereas the present target is an untrialed downstream interventional mean in a randomized multi-policy SCM with action-dependent selective labels.

Breakdown-frontier inference concerns robustness regions indexed by assumption relaxations; it does not supply the structural SLCC observable--target polytope or the label-coarsening dual-face criterion.

Calibrated projection gives uniformly asymptotically valid intervals for scalar projections in moment equality and inequality models; the paper's whole-set confidence construction is a distinct finite multinomial propagation result.

The directional delta method covers Hadamard directionally differentiable maps and convex-set projection; the mass-aware paired endpoint-face composition is specialized here, while the separate atomic subsampling specialization remains under active-cone repair.
The numerical delta method offers an alternative route for directionally differentiable maps but does not give the exact SLCC dual-face refinement criterion.

The paper documents failures of bootstrap and m-out-of-n endpoint procedures in moment-inequality settings; it motivates, but does not validate, the paper's separate centered atomic-tie subsampling calculation.

tldr: Repeated trials cannot accompany every updated human--AI policy, and in pretrial applications ground truth is revealed only by an endogenous action. The proposal identifies the exact observable--target image of legal finite response types and makes a complete three-performance, two-arm, thirty-two-type quotient the novelty kernel. Its full twelve-cell laws lie in the relative interior of the actual observable polytope and give \([1/2,3/4]\) versus the label-blind \([1/4,1]\), with a perturbed law giving \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\). Continuity yields a relatively open region of two-sided strict refinement. Generic simultaneous multinomial confidence-region propagation supplies a finite-sample implementation corollary. Euclidean projection yields a projection-composed directional limit, while conservative centered \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) quantiles at atomic simultaneous ties remain the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 does not claim tightness under its unit-level restrictions and treats only a restricted missing-label mechanism. DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 supplies generic finite response-function optimization and confidence-region propagation, but not the legal action-dependent selective-label quotient or a strict full-versus-blind region.
project_justification.niche: A three-performance design makes the trialed low and high configurations bracket an untrialed middle configuration in opposite directions according to latent correctness, so selective revelation of truth can have a stable two-sided identifying value.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact finite-response converse, exhausts the full model by thirty-two legal observable--target representatives, verifies a strictly positive full-polytope mixture with exact endpoint arithmetic, derives the relative-open two-sided refinement, and separates generic finite-sample propagation from the new boundary limit and atomic-quantile question.

technical_internal_limitation: The full-model certificate includes legal realization and actual relative interior. The remaining internal bottleneck is inference at an observable-law projection face when both LPs have multiple optimal bases and the joint directional limit has atoms; weak conditional convergence alone need not validate the required quantile.
honest_scope: The identification results concern finite strata and policies, three distinct certified performance levels in the strictness certificate, and binary actions, labels, and outcomes. Certified performance values are external inputs. Generic confidence-region propagation is used as an implementation result. The projection-composed limit is pointwise, and atomic tie-inclusive subsampling validity is open. Equality of the untrialed and a trialed configuration recovers the randomized observed mean. Full revelation of \(Z\) removes masking but does not identify a distinct untrialed configuration. Multiclass actions, dynamic policies, violation budgets, joint deployment targets, and policy learning remain outside this kernel.
